name: Shape-memory stomach coil
subtitle: a swallowed capsule that fills the stomach

effects.effect: a bent metal returns to its remembered shape at body heat, and goes limp when chilled

effect: a bent metal returns to its remembered shape at body heat, and goes limp when chilled
how: Stomach balloons help people eat less, but they are put in and taken out with a tube down the throat. This one is a capsule holding a coiled wire of shape-memory metal: at body heat it springs into a loose cage the size of a fist that sits in the stomach and makes a small meal feel big. Months later a glass of ice water chills it below its switching point so it goes limp and passes out.
obstacle: Making sure a soft metal coil never snags, kinks or slips into the bowel before it's meant to.
why: Removal by a cold drink avoids a second endoscopy; safety in the gut is the big unknown.
real: Swallowable self-expanding gastric devices exist but use balloons or hydrogels (Elipse, Plenity, US8287562); intragastric implants with Nitinol collapsible frames are only patented, not swallowable.
